summary: Grade C / 66 分 —— 分红很好，价格不好。0% 英国预扣税（HK 个人 gross = net，是本组合税务效率最高的标的之一），FY2025 DPS 66p (+8.2%)、FY2026 公司明确指引 70p (+6.1%)，派息率连续四年稳定在 ~38.4%，低于其自设 40-60% 政策区间下限；FCF 覆盖 1.51x（三年合计 1.37x），且后剔除利息/少数股东，口径保守；DRIP 为市场购股、零摊薄，£20 亿回购已于 2026-06-26 完成、流通股 4,047m→4,007m (-1.0%)。红利陷阱清单全项通过，Value-trap veto 未触发；即使 Bear 情景 FY2028 仍有 1.03x 覆盖 —— 是"冻结"而非"削减"。但入场价不达标：股价 12 个月自 1,288.6p 低点上涨 52%，前瞻股息率被压到 3.57%，低于本框架对该风险级别要求的 4.5% 下限，较公允上限 1,600p 高出 22.5%。三项新增风险来自 2026-07-28 Q2 业绩与 7-15 完成的 Nuvalent 收购：(1) 净负债 £15.1bn → pro-forma ~£22bn（约 1.9-2.0x Core EBITDA），四年去杠杆趋势逆转；(2) camlipixant 减值 £13 亿，且回购完成后无后继计划；(3) 20-F 专利表确认 Trelegy（£30 亿、+13%）美国专利 2027 年到期、已被 Transpire 提起 ANDA 挑战 —— 比 dolutegravir 悬崖更早。dolutegravir 家族（美 2028/欧 2029，约 £58 亿）风险真实但对冲扎实：cabotegravir 长效针剂受保护至 2031、£18.4 亿 +46%、已占美国 HIV 销售 30%，且 Shionogi 或有对价（半年 £7.1 亿）随 DTG 销售同步下降，形成天然现金流对冲。结论：优质收息标的，但按红利收益率框架当前"过贵"；Fair 1,200-1,600p、Accumulate 1,133-1,200p、Strong buy <=1,133p（ADR 约 $32.4-43.2 / <=$30.6）。注：以盈利口径看 GSK 并不贵（约 10.8x FY2026E Core EPS），差异源于低派息政策而非分红安全性。

Grade B / 78 分 —— 优质资产，价格不便宜。分红引擎是全球银行中最干净的之一（ROE 24.5%、CET1 12.3%、payout 72%、五年零增发零 scrip 零债务融资派息），派息总额从 2021 年 R$70.7 亿增至 2025 年 R$337.0 亿、4 年 4.8 倍。但**巴西在 2026-01-01 同时开征 10% 股息预扣税（Law 15,270/2025，此前三十年为零）并把 JCP 预扣税从 15% 提到 17.5%（Complementary Law 224/2025）**，HK 持有人的混合实际税率从 6.1% 跳到 **13.05%**；同期股价 12 个月 +24%。结果是毛收益率与 2025 年持平在 7.6%，净收益率却掉了 90bp 到 **6.3%** —— 差额被巴西财政部拿走。第二个关键结构：**59% 的分红来自每年 11 月董事会自由裁量、无公式化政策的年末特别股息**（2023 年首次 R$110 亿 → 2025 年 R$200 亿），而经常性 JCP 被 TJLP×净资产的税法上限锁死，四年只从 R$1.117 增到 R$1.243/股（+11%）—— 派息增长的全部弹性集中在自由裁量部分，这是必要收益率必须上调的首要理由。第三是覆盖度的真实约束：FY2025 赚 R$468 亿派 R$337 亿，同期 RWA 增 9.2% 需留存 R$155 亿，实际只留存 R$131 亿并回购注销 R$30 亿，**CET1 资本绝对额从 R$1,883 亿降到 R$1,856 亿、比率从 13.7% 降到 12.3%（−140bp）** —— 72% payout 略高于有机可持续的约 70%，差额由缓冲填补；剩余可释放缓冲约 80bp / R$120 亿（管理层反复以 CET1 11.5% 为管理参照）。可持续 payout 对 RWA 增速极敏感：+6% → 78%，+8% → 70.7%，+10% → 63.4%，因此 Bear 情景不需要假设利润下滑，只需假设增长变快。正面证据同样扎实：90 天 NPL 1.9% 连续 6 季持平于历史最优、巴西效率比 1H26 35.2% 为历史最佳、1H26 净利 R$246.9 亿 +9.1%、Tier1 13.8% / LCR 202% / NSFR 122%、无 scrip 无 ATM 无 DRIP、2025-11 实质注销 7,885 万股 PN（R$30 亿）。送红股（2025-03 送 10%、2025-12 送 3%）不是 scrip、不构成稀释，但使历史每股数据须除以 1.133 才可比 —— 本报告全部 DPS 用「派息总额÷当前股数」还原，且**不使用任何第三方派息数据**（Yahoo 的 ITUB 序列遗漏了 2025-12-19 那笔 R$1.868/股 主力派息）。估值：N = 净 **$0.53/ADR**（`mid_cycle`，三项正常化：利润 R$545→520 亿剔除信贷成本历史最优与 Selic 浮存溢价、payout 73%→70%、汇率 5.084→5.25 因 BRL 12 个月已升值 12%）；B = 净 $0.40（FY2027 Bear：信贷成本 +R$50 亿、RWA +11% 迫使 payout 降至 62%、BRL 贬至 5.80）；r 取 **7.0%–9.0%**，自「强银行」5–7% 档上调 200bp。Fair **$5.89–7.57**、Accumulate $4.44–5.89、Strong buy ≤$4.44 —— **现价 $7.94 高于 Fair 上沿 4.9%，对应正常化净收益率 6.68%**。Value-trap veto **未触发**。结论稳健但不极端：若 r 放宽到 6.5%–8.5%，Fair 上沿升至 $8.15，现价进入区间。**最值得落实的缺口**：香港在巴西 IN RFB 1037 避税地名单上，JCP 法定税率 25%，本报告假设 ADR 存托行（美国）层级适用 17.5% —— 若为 25%，N 降至 $0.49、Fair 上沿降至 $7.00，需用一份真实券商流水验证。持有可以，加仓等 $7.57 以下。

summary: Grade D / 51 分 —— **2026 年 Pfizer 冻结了股息，终结 2011–2025 连续 15 年的提息记录**，这是全篇最重要的单一事实。2025-12-12 董事会宣布 Q1 2026 季息维持 $0.43，Q2、Q3 继续维持；冻结发生在 FY2025 调整后 EPS 同比 +4% 的一年之后，说明这不是被当期业绩逼出来的，而是管理层前瞻性地为 2027–28 专利悬崖与 $515 亿净债务保留现金。6.43% 的毛息率经 **30% 美国预扣税**（无美港税收协定，W-8BEN 无法降低）后只剩 **4.50% 净**，每年漏损约占本金 1.93%。**覆盖度是第二个问题**：FY2023 0.52x、FY2024 1.03x、FY2025 0.93x —— 三年里两年 FCF 无法覆盖股息；根源是 FY2025 调整后净利 $184 亿却只产出 $117 亿经营现金流（转化率仅 64%，FY2024 为 72%），因此任何只看 payout ratio（FY2025 为调整后 EPS 的 53%）的分析都会得出错误的安全结论。**第三是 2028 悬崖**：公司口径 2026–2030 约 $170–180 亿年收入面临专利到期，约占 FY2025 收入 62.6bn 的 **28%**（Eliquis $79.6 亿、Prevnar $64.9 亿、Vyndaqel $43.7 亿、Ibrance $23.6 亿、Xtandi $19.4 亿），Eliquis 欧洲独占已于 2026-05 到期、美国 2026–2028 视诉讼而定。分红结构本身是全档案最干净的之一：零特别股息、无 scrip、无 ATM、无 FX 错配，五年股数 5,708M→5,699M 几乎不动。但**回购三年为零**（$33 亿授权未动用，公司明确先去杠杆后回购），股东回报 100% 来自需缴 30% 税的股息、零来自免税的股份注销。并购记录是最弱一环：Seagen $430 亿之后，Q2 2026 一次性计提 **$43 亿减值**（sigvotatug vedotin $38 亿因二线 NSCLC 三期数据不利、Oxbryta $5.25 亿），danuglipron 已终止，Metsera 在与 Novo 的公开竞价中从自报 $47.50/股 加到 $65.60/股 + 最高 $20.65 CVR。正面证据也真实存在：H1 2026 经营现金流 $34.5 亿、**同比 +97%**（H1 2025 仅 $17.5 亿，H1 2024 为 −$6.9 亿，注意 Pfizer 现金流极度偏重下半年，H1 数据不可年化）；成本计划累计 **$82 亿**（成本重整 $67 亿 + 制造优化 $15 亿，至 2029）；FY2026 指引收入上调至 $605–625 亿、调整后 EPS 维持 $2.80–3.00；肥胖症管线 PF'3944 (MET-097i) VESPER-1 28 周安慰剂调整后减重 14.1%、2026 年启动 10 项三期、目标 2028 上市。因此 Fundamental Trend 判为 **Transformation / High Uncertainty** —— 不是 Structural Decline（管理层在大规模再投资而非收割，故 Grade C 上限与买入区间暂停规则不适用），也绝不是 Stable。**估值的核心判断**：中周期可分配现金约 $77.5 亿 ÷ 5,800M 股 只支持毛 DPS **$1.40**，比申报的 $1.72 低 19%，所以 N = 净 $0.98（`mid_cycle`，已剔除每年约 $20 亿的资产负债表流动性补贴 —— 该来源按定义不可经常化，$117 亿流动性最多撑 3–4 年且与去杠杆冲突）；B = 净 $0.735，来自 FY2028 Bear 可分配现金仅 $23–43 亿的推导；r 取 **5.5%–7.0%**（比档案内 VZ 的 5.0%–6.5% 上移 50bp，因覆盖、增长记录、可预测性三项均劣于 VZ）。Fair $14.00–17.82、Accumulate $10.50–14.00、Strong Buy ≤$10.50 —— **现价 $26.76 高于公允上沿 50.2%，需下跌 33.4% 才进入合理持有区**。结论对输入稳健：即便改用申报 DPS $1.72 与最宽松的 5.0%–6.5%，公允上沿也只有 $24.08，仍贵 11%。**Dividend and Yield Runway 九个情景格中，税后收益率只在 3.14%–4.60% 之间移动 —— 连 FY2028 Bull 都够不到 5.5% 的所需下限**，而 Base 情景下股息占可分配现金的比例从 FY2026 的 101% 升至 FY2028 的 143%（且已含每年 $20 亿补贴）。Value-trap veto **未触发**，但这是本档案最接近触发的标的：两项黄灯（正常化 FCF 覆盖 <1.0x、申报 DPS 高于中周期产能）已通过把 N 下调 19% 计入估值，而非用暂停估值来回避；不否决的依据是恢复路径有证据（$82 亿成本计划 + H1 OCF +97% + $117 亿流动性 + 投资级信用 + 管理层选择冻结而非举债提息）。价格位置中性（三年中位数 $26.59 上方 0.6%，52 周区间 $23.58–28.75，Q2 业绩后四个交易日 +6.9%），6.43% 毛息率在五年跨度属高位但在近三年只是约 40 分位 —— 并不便宜。Portfolio Role 从 D 档默认的『高风险收息/特殊情境』覆盖为 **Watchlist**：24 个月内减派概率低，问题是价格没有安全边际与 2028 悬崖未解，而非迫在眉睫的困境。跟踪三个变量：(1) 每季 OCF 与转化率（唯一能同时抬升 N 并解除黄灯、且每季可验证的变量）；(2) **2026 年 12 月的 Q1 2027 股息申报** —— 若连续第二年冻结，五年稳定性模块须降档，Grade 将跌破 50；(3) PF'3944 三期读出 —— 唯一能把 Fundamental Trend 推向任一极端、届时模型须整体重建的单一事件。预扣税为 `market_default` 假设，非 broker-observed（未提供 PFE 券商流水）。

Grade B - a near-unimpeachable dividend attached to a disqualifying yield, and waiting will not fix it. **The last twelve months contain a Strait-of-Hormuz windfall**: Q2 2026 alone earned $12.07bn / $6.11 diluted EPS at $104 Brent versus $2.21bn / $1.11 in Q1 at $81; Brent touched ~$120 in April and is back to $79-82 today, so every TTM figure is a peak-cycle artifact and everything here is normalized at **$70 Brent mid-cycle**. The dividend itself: **39 consecutive annual increases** (+4% to $1.78/qtr in Jan 2026, $7.12 annualized), zero special or variable payouts, no scrip, no ATM, and cash dividends covered by free cash flow in **every one of the last five years** (worst 1.27x in 2024); the 2025 accounting payout hit 104% of net income as post-Hess DD&A rose to $11.9bn annualized, yet cash cover was still 1.30x - only the cash measure is honest for this company. The balance sheet is the real moat: net debt ratio 15.6%->**13.1%**, net debt/CFFO **0.6x**, a record **$8.4bn** of total debt retired in Q2 alone, and leverage sitting below its own 20-25% target with an estimated ~$25bn of headroom. The key structural point: **the buyback is the shock absorber and the dividend sits behind it** - in 2023-25 dividends plus buybacks exceeded FCF by ~$6.5bn/$12.0bn/$10.5bn, all funded from the cash balance and debt, while **the dividend itself was never debt-funded**; across six single-driver sensitivities the derived DPS does not move once, every shock lands on the repurchase line. Nor is the asset base in decline: production +20% y/y (H1 3,965 MBOED), and in 2024->2025 Brent fell $12 while recurring FCF rose $15.0bn->$16.6bn on Hess consolidation, TCO's FGP flipping from capex sink to cash distributor, and cost cuts; $3bn of structural savings landed six months early, Hess synergies hit $1.5bn (150% of target), guidance is >10% annual adjusted-FCF growth at a flat $70 Brent reaching $28-30bn by 2030, with capex held at the $18-19bn floor. **But 30% US withholding** (no US-HK treaty; W-8BEN gives no rate relief) cuts a 3.77% headline gross yield to **2.64% net** - a permanent ~$4.2m/yr loss per $1bn invested that a DRIP cannot avoid, since reinvestment occurs on the after-tax amount. Across all nine scenario cells in section 13 the after-tax yield on today's cost moves only between **2.64% and 2.98%** - three years out, including the Bull case, it never reaches 3%. N=$4.984 net (mid_cycle @$70 Brent, stripping the $92 H1 realization, the $104 Q2 quarter, $1.4bn of Q2 timing effects and $1.8bn of FY2025 asset sales), B=N because the Bear outcome is a **freeze, not a cut** ($15.9-16.4bn of distributable cash against a $14.2bn dividend cost at $55-58 Brent, with 2020 as precedent when debt went $23.7bn->$42.8bn to maintain and raise the payout), so the accumulation band is **empty**; r 7.0-9.5% net (the cyclical floor, not pushed lower because Forecast Confidence is only Medium). Fair/hold $52.46-71.20, strong buy <=$52.46. At $188.63 the stock sits **2.65x above** the fair upper bound and would have to fall 62.3% to enter it - and $52.46 is precisely the March 2020 COVID low. The conflict worth stating plainly: a 7-9.5% required net yield implies a 10.0-13.6% required gross yield at this withholding rate, which Chevron has touched once in fifty years; even tax-free the required gross yield implies $75-102, and an AA-rated major does not yield 9% gross outside a solvency panic. The conclusion is not that the framework is wrong or the company is bad - Chevron's shareholder return is deliberately built as ~2.6% net dividend + ~3% share retirement + >10% FCF growth at flat $70 Brent, a total-return proposition in which the dividend is by design the smallest part. Veto **not triggered** - the risk is overpaying, not a dividend cut. Grade stays B (the business earns it); Portfolio Role overridden to **Watchlist** because the after-tax income mandate is not met. The highest-value fix is not timing but holding structure: removing the 30% withholding lifts the yield from 2.64% to 3.77% and the fair ceiling from $71 to $102. Also watch the deliberate increase in political-risk exposure (Iraq West Qurna 2 / Nasiriyah heads of agreement, a publicly courted Venezuela re-entry) and the one variable most likely to rewrite this analysis favourably - the 20-year, 2.67GW Microsoft West Texas data-centre PPA. Withholding is `market_default`-assumed, not broker-observed.

summary: Supersedes the 2026-07-31 report. Fundamental verdict, N=$2.02, B=$1.98, score 75/B and the untriggered veto all carry over unchanged; the one substantive change is that the required net yield is tightened from 4.5-5.5% to 5.0-6.5%, moving the fair upper bound (the add-trigger) from $44.89 down to $40.40. Two reasons: (i) buy-zone.md requires a conservative balance sheet to justify a downward adjustment, and that is precisely the one condition VZ fails - net unsecured leverage 2.5x versus its own 2.0-2.25x target, ~$158.2bn total debt, $7.35bn LTM interest - so there is no basis for pushing r_low below the 5% telecom floor; (ii) this framework anchors on after-tax dividend income, and folding the tax-free buyback yield into a required dividend yield mixes two measures - buyback value belongs in the total-return narrative instead. The quality verdict is unchanged: 30% US withholding turns a 6.06% headline gross yield into 4.24% net, the single biggest structural drag for an HK holder, and that is the lowest after-tax income yield since 2021. The dividend itself is close to unimpeachable - 20 straight annual increases (+2.5% to $0.7075/qtr, announced Jan 2026, effective from the May payment), no scrip, no ATM, five years of cumulative FCF $92.0bn covering cumulative dividends $55.0bn (1.67x), with not one year funded by debt, asset sales or issuance. 2026 is a genuine inflection under Dan Schulman: 2Q26 adjusted EBITDA $13.7bn (+7.2%) and 40.1% margin both all-time records, 1H26 FCF $10.2bn (+16.0%), the first positive Q1 postpaid phone net adds since 2013, postpaid phone churn 0.97%->0.92%, broadband at 17.1m connections after the Frontier close on 2026-01-20 ($9.8bn cash + $12.9bn assumed debt), a $9bn opex/capex savings programme, buybacks cutting shares 4,217m->4,155m (-1.5%) in six months with the 2026 target raised to $4.5bn, plus a $1bn+ Google dark-fiber contract. Guidance raised twice: FY26 FCF $21.9-22.1bn (+9-10%), adj EPS $4.99-5.04, capex $16.0-16.5bn. The catch: 2Q26 wireless service revenue still -0.7%, total revenue -0.7%, GAAP net income -22.9%, leverage 2.2x->2.5x, and a reported but unsigned ~$10bn EchoStar AWS-3 spectrum deal (first reported by Bloomberg in Sep 2025) that would defer deleveraging by ~2 years and force buybacks to pause - carried as a standalone persistent sensitivity (accumulation bound -$1.40), excluded from Base. Because buybacks shrink the count, dividend cash cost is locked at ~$11.8bn in all nine scenario cells - per-share growth is entirely self-funded by share retirement, so the durability of DPS growth depends on the buyback continuing; even in Bear (FCF $20.0bn, $6bn/yr debt paydown) the payout is 84% of distributable cash and 59% of FCF, so the rational cut is the buyback, not the dividend - which is why B sits only 2% below N and the accumulation band is nearly empty. Fair/hold $31.08-40.40, accumulate 30.46-31.08, strong buy <=30.46. At $46.70 the stock sits 15.6% above the fair upper bound (4.0% above on the prior calibration). The structural point worth stating plainly: the strong-buy boundary implies a 9.51% gross yield, which VZ has approached only once - the October 2023 lead-cable panic at ~8.8% - so the accumulation band is in practice near-unreachable, correctly reflecting that a US ordinary share is a structurally inefficient vehicle for an HK taxable income mandate. Veto not triggered - the risk is overpaying, not a dividend cut. Hold if owned (~6.55% total after-tax shareholder yield including the 2.31% untaxed buyback); reassess adding below $40.40. Withholding is legal_structure-assumed, not broker-observed.

summary: Grade B core income — quality yes, price no. The 30% US withholding turns a 6.14% headline gross yield into 4.30% net for an HK holder, the single biggest structural drag. The dividend itself is close to unimpeachable: 20 straight annual increases (latest +2.5% to $0.7075/qtr in Jan 2026), no scrip, no ATM, and five years of cumulative FCF $92.0bn covering cumulative dividends $55.0bn (1.67x) with not one year funded by debt, asset sales or issuance — debt growth financed spectrum and M&A, never the payout. 2026 is a genuine inflection under Dan Schulman: 2Q26 adjusted EBITDA $13.7bn (+7.2%) and 40.1% margin are both all-time records, 1H26 FCF $10.2bn (+16.0%), postpaid phone churn 0.97%->0.92%, broadband at 17.1m connections after the Frontier close on 2026-01-20 ($9.8bn cash + $12.9bn assumed debt), a $9bn opex/capex savings programme, and the first real buyback in years — shares 4,217m->4,155m (-1.5%) in six months, 2026 target raised to $4.5bn. Guidance raised twice this year: FY26 FCF $21.9-22.1bn (+9-10%), adj EPS $4.99-5.04, capex $16.0-16.5bn. The catch: wireless service revenue guided ~flat, total revenue -0.7% in 2Q26, GAAP net income -22.9%, net unsecured debt/EBITDA up 2.2x->2.5x on Frontier, LTM interest expense $7.35bn, and a reported but unsigned ~$10bn EchoStar AWS-3 spectrum deal that would defer deleveraging and buybacks. Because buybacks shrink the count, total dividend cash cost stays flat at ~$11.7bn across all three scenarios — per-share growth is self-funded; even in Bear (FCF $18.5bn, $5bn/yr debt paydown) the payout is 92% of distributable cash, so the rational cut is the buyback, not the dividend.
